text:
A: Hello? Can you hear me? Sorry, I'm not very good with these.
B: Yeah, I can hear you.
A: Oh good. Erm, I'm Alison. I'm up in Chester-le-Street, it's near Durham.
B: Callum. Basingstoke.
A: Basingstoke. I don't think I've ever been. Is it nice?
B: It's alright. Bunch of roundabouts. Bit dead.
A: Well, we've got plenty of them up here too. Erm. Did you do the puzzle bit? I found that quite hard. I don't know if I did it right.
B: Yeah, it was fine. Bit long.
A: Are you at college, or...?
B: Sixth form. Doing A-levels. Business, Economics and PE.
A: Oh, that's a good mix. Are you thinking of uni?
B: Nah. Not paying nine grand to sit in a room. I want to do a degree apprenticeship, like at a bank or something. You get paid and you get the degree, so it just makes more sense, to be fair.
A: That does sound sensible, actually. Do you work as well?
B: Yeah, sports shop. Trainers mostly. Saturdays.
A: Oh right. Is that busy?
B: Dead till about eleven and then it's chaos. Everyone comes in at once.
A: I bet. I used to work in a school office and it was a bit like that. Quiet, quiet, then three parents on the phone and one at the window.
B: Right.
A: Sorry, I've gone off on one there. Erm. Do you like it?
B: It's alright. I'm better on the floor than most of them, to be honest. I sell the most socks and that, the add-ons. And I resell trainers on the side as well. You use your staff discount or get them on release day and then flip them. I had a pair go for nearly double what I paid.
A: Double? Goodness. How do you know which ones'll go up?
B: You just kind of know. You watch the releases, see what's hyped. And you've got to check they're not fakes if you're buying, cause loads are. Stitching, the box label, the smell even.
A: The smell! I wouldn't have thought of that.
B: Yeah, fakes smell like glue. Proper strong.
A: Well, you sound like you know what you're doing. Our Danny would've loved that. He was always on about trainers at your age.
B: Yeah.
A: He's in Leeds now. Erm, he's twenty-six.
B: Nice.
A: I'm not working at the moment. I left the school a couple of years ago. It all went a bit... computers and targets. I might do something part-time eventually.
B: Fair enough.
A: I don't know if that's the sort of thing we're meant to talk about.
B: Dunno. Don't think it matters. It's three minutes.
A: That's true. Do you play football? I saw the Arsenal shirt behind you.
B: Yeah, five-a-side Wednesdays. Used to play Sunday league but I quit. Arsenal's my dad's team, so.
A: My husband's Sunderland. He'd tell you all about it. I just ask the score.
B: Sunderland, yeah. They've had it rough, to be fair.
A: Don't tell him that.
B: Nah, I won't. Has he been going long, like season ticket, or
